findings.rationale:
Evidence: api-app/src/integrations/meta/meta.client.spec.ts:163-172 supplies app_id different-app together with only whatsapp_business_management and no messaging granular grant. api-app/src/integrations/meta/meta.client.ts:94-100 independently enforces app equality, required scopes, validity, and a nonempty WABA intersection. The only other app_id negative in the current spec is a non-string shape case at :254, which exercises the parser rather than semantic audience equality. A scoped search of the public src/test MetaHttpClient call sites found no separate otherwise-valid wrong-app negative. The real-adapter BFF bridge at test/number-onboarding-flow.e2e-spec.ts:156-184 uses a matching app and tests malformed JSON/grant shape.

Why now: this is a concrete test-assurance blind spot at the changed grant-validation boundary, central to D-02. Removing only the semantic app-equality condition would still leave the existing different-app test rejected by the missing messaging authorization/WABA intersection. All remaining current real-adapter fixtures either match the app or fail structural parsing. The new cp36i revoked-grant case correctly isolates is_valid:false, but it does not isolate audience equality. The production guard is present and correct on inspection; no exploit or runtime defect is claimed, and no mutation/test run was performed by this reviewer. The complete current TQA is terminal and favorable, but its general coverage-sufficiency conclusion does not establish this particular negative.

Options A/B/C:
A. Add one dedicated wrong-app unit case against MetaHttpClient with is_valid:true, both required scopes, intersecting granular WABA targets, a scoped token, and a valid matching phone-page fallback. Assert the same rejection's real class and catalog code, exactly one fixed-host/app-auth debug request, and zero phone-number requests. Effort: small; risk: low; blast radius: one unit test; maintenance: low; performance: one local mocked call; elegance: explicit fault isolation; structural soundness: retains the real boundary and no production workaround. Recommended.
B. Parameterize the current isolated semantic-invalid-grant test into distinct revoked and wrong-app rows, each with all unrelated fields valid. Effort: small; risk: low but includes test refactoring; blast radius: the unit spec; maintenance: potentially less fixture duplication; performance: equivalent; elegance/structure: acceptable if the two fault oracles remain explicit.
C. Accept the current code after an explicit assurance-debt disposition based on the inspected production guard, while narrowing claims that audience rejection is independently regression-tested. Effort: minimal; risk: this critical guard can regress without a discriminating test; blast radius: future cross-app grant acceptance; maintenance: tracked debt; performance: unchanged; elegance/structure: production unchanged but protection incomplete. This is more defensible for a tightly bounded private checkpoint than an unqualified coverage claim, but weaker than A.

Recommendation: A as bounded coverage of already-correct approved behavior, with no fabricated RED or production change. Resolve this finding explicitly before treating the final local assurance gate as unqualified. Refresh only affected evidence, preserve honest build-neutral consumer reuse where justified, and let the root apply the existing review/adjudication workflow.
